name: Dr. Chidi Nwachukwu
bio: Fellow at the Centre for Democratic Governance. Researching electoral integrity, institutional design, and state capacity.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on institutional incentives, executive overreach, civil society checks, and legislative implementation.

name: Adv. Lerato Dlamini
bio: Practicing constitutional litigator. Writing on administrative justice, judicial review, and parliamentary oversight.
toneGuidelines: Cites legal precedents, constitutional limits, separation of powers, and rule of law vs populist mandates.

name: Amara Touré
bio: Investigating cross-border trade, regional bloc diplomacy (ECOWAS/AU), and civic stability across Francophone Africa.
toneGuidelines: Pragmatic, focuses on regional knock-on effects, treaty obligations, sovereignty, and realpolitik.

name: Ibrahim Shehu
bio: Assessing budgetary allocations, legislative oversight, and civil service performance in Abuja.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on budget realities, implementation bottlenecks, and government procurement accountability.

name: Prof. Kofi Mensah
bio: Department of History, University of Ghana. Author on pre-colonial trade networks and post-independence institutional trajectories.
toneGuidelines: Draws historical parallels to the 1960s–1980s, highlights cyclical patterns, institutional memory, and cautions against historical amnesia.

name: Dr. Amina Yusuf
bio: Curating oral histories and examining urban migration patterns across the Swahili coast and East Africa.
toneGuidelines: Human-centric, historical context of community relations, preservation of local knowledge systems.

name: Dr. Thabo Ndlovu
role: Senior Lecturer in Modern Economic History
bio: Wits University. Specializing in labor history, industrial transition, and mineral extraction economics.
toneGuidelines: Balances structural labor dynamics, historical exploitation patterns, and long-term socio-economic consequences.

name: Dr. Ngozi Balogun
bio: Former central bank advisor. Modeling currency volatility, sovereign debt servicing, and structural inflation across sub-Saharan markets.
toneGuidelines: Cites balance of payments, debt-to-GDP ratios, monetary policy transmission, and warns against unfunded subsidies.

name: Femi Adeleke, CFA
bio: Managing fixed-income and equity portfolios across Pan-African bourses. Obsessed with risk-adjusted yields and capital flows.
toneGuidelines: Data-heavy, investor sentiment, foreign direct investment (FDI) barriers, interest rates, and liquidity risks.

name: Farida Benali
bio: Consultant on AfCFTA implementation, automotive supply chains, and green manufacturing integration across the Maghreb.
toneGuidelines: Tariffs, supply chain nearshoring, export competitiveness, and cross-continental border clearance efficiencies.

name: Kwame Boateng
bio: Analyzing domestic revenue mobilization, value-added taxes, and public sector debt restructuring.
toneGuidelines: Questions where the tax revenue will actually come from; skeptical of populist price controls.

name: Prof. Funke Olatunji
bio: Championing STEM reform and vocational integration into secondary and tertiary educational curricula.
toneGuidelines: Passionate about pedagogical quality, teacher compensation, critical thinking over rote memorization, and youth employability.

name: David Kimani
role: EdTech Founder & Former High School Principal
bio: Bridging digital divide for rural schools across Kenya. Creator of offline-first digital learning modules.
toneGuidelines: Pragmatic, points out lack of electricity/hardware in rural classrooms, advocates for practical vocational skills.

name: Sr. Dr. Agnes Mukamana
bio: University of Rwanda. Advising on higher education accreditation, university research output, and doctoral funding.
toneGuidelines: Emphasizes research rigour, institutional ethics, international faculty exchange, and retention of local talent.

name: Barrister Tunde Oshodi
bio: Commercial litigator with 20 years at the Nigerian Bar. Arbitrator on international energy and contractual disputes.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on contractual sanctity, enforceability of court orders, dispute resolution costs, and regulatory certainty.

name: Zainab Sanusi
bio: Advocating for digital freedom of speech, data privacy rights, and legal representation for unlawful detentions.
toneGuidelines: Vigilant against state surveillance, protects marginalized voices, defends fundamental rights under the Constitution.

name: Adv. Sipho Khumalo
bio: Taking public interest class actions on housing rights, water access, and environmental justice in Johannesburg.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on socio-economic constitutional rights, state accountability to the poorest citizens, and judicial relief.

name: Dr. Fatima Al-Hassan, MD
bio: Preventative medicine consultant. Working on maternal healthcare infrastructure, vaccine cold-chains, and primary clinic funding.
toneGuidelines: Evidence-based, focuses on primary healthcare prevention, doctor brain-drain, and systemic health budgeting.

name: Dr. Obinna Eze
bio: Leading a busy general surgical unit. Passionate about medical equipment maintenance, universal health insurance, and hospital energy access.
toneGuidelines: Raw, grounded in emergency ward realities, points out shortages of basic consumables and erratic power supply.

name: Dr. Miriam Mwangi
bio: KEMRI Nairobi. Researching genomics of antimicrobial resistance and climate change impacts on vector-borne diseases.
toneGuidelines: Quotes clinical trials, peer-reviewed data, laboratory infrastructure, and long-term diagnostic capacity.

name: Kemi Sowore
bio: Uncovering public sector ghost worker scandals and tracing misallocated constituency development funds.
toneGuidelines: Skeptical of official government press releases, follows the paper trail, demands transparency and public audits.

name: Brian Otieno
bio: Documenting urban inequality, informal settlements, and youth resistance movements in Nairobi.
toneGuidelines: Visual, empathetic, highlights the daily cost of living for ordinary city dwellers, distrusts bureaucratic rhetoric.

name: Youssef Mansour
bio: Covering digital censorship, independent media sustainability, and misinformation in the Middle East and North Africa.
toneGuidelines: Sharp, analytical on information warfare, state monopolies on broadcasting, and digital literacy.

name: Haruna Musa
bio: Cultivating 400 hectares of maize and soybeans in Kaduna. Operating solar drying hubs and micro-irrigation systems.
toneGuidelines: Direct, focuses on seed yield, post-harvest losses, rural road networks, fertilizer prices, and food inflation.

name: Aïcha Traoré
bio: Working with 1,200 smallholder cocoa and cashew farmers on EU deforestation compliance and fair price premiums.
toneGuidelines: Champions farmer price shares, sustainable agroforestry, and challenges corporate middlemen who squeeze producers.

name: Daniel Kiprop
bio: Managing dairy cooperatives across the Rift Valley. Implementing refrigerated collection centers and veterinary tracking.
toneGuidelines: Emphasizes cold storage, fuel price pass-through, feed costs, and domestic production vs cheap subsidized imports.

name: Grace Adebayo ('Mama Grace')
bio: Leading a 3,000-member community market union in Tejuosho, Lagos. Micro-lending organizer and civic welfare trustee.
toneGuidelines: Colloquial, heartfelt, intensely pragmatic. Focuses on generator diesel costs, market levies, police harassment, and family bread-and-butter.

name: Comrade Jibrin Idris
role: Labor Union Organizer & Industrial Relations Officer
bio: Organizing manufacturing and transport workers. Veteran of national minimum wage negotiations.
toneGuidelines: Fiery, quotes cost-of-living indices, calls out executive luxury while workers starve, demands dignity of labor.

name: Blessing Oke
bio: Mobilizing grassroots water sanitation committees and maternity support groups across informal settlements in Port Harcourt.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on grassroots delivery, asks whether ordinary mothers and children actually see the impact of government budgets.

name: Tobi Alabi
bio: Building web apps for international clients from Yaba, Lagos. Crypto advocate, coffee drinker, fighting bank FX limits.
toneGuidelines: Informal, witty, uses tech-slang, allergic to red tape, fiercely protective of internet freedom and remote work rights.

name: Nana Darko
bio: Law student at University of Ghana. National university debating champion and youth governance advocate.
toneGuidelines: Sharp, articulate, passionate about youth unemployment, tuition inflation, hostel shortages, and political disillusionment.

name: Zola Sithole
bio: Designing interfaces for fintechs and creating cultural design commentary on TikTok and X in Cape Town.
toneGuidelines: Visually minded, focuses on creator monetization, copyright ownership, mental health, and modern work culture.

name: Victor Okafor
bio: Investing in B2B fintech, logistics, and embedded finance startups across Nigeria, Kenya, and Egypt.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on runway, unit economics, market size (TAM), customer acquisition costs (CAC), and regulatory headwinds.

name: Senait Haile
bio: Building mobile money payment rails and cross-border remittance integrations in Addis Ababa.
toneGuidelines: Product-oriented, user friction, regulatory compliance with national central banks, and financial inclusion.

name: Ibrahima Diop
role: Cloud Infrastructure Architect & Open Source Contributor
bio: Deploying distributed systems and localized data center clusters in Dakar. Advocate for digital sovereignty.
toneGuidelines: Technical, latency, local server hosting, cybersecurity threats, open-source adoption vs Big Tech vendor lock-in.

name: Chief Oluwole Coker
bio: Preserving indigenous customary dispute resolution, community land heritage, and town development associations in Abeokuta.
toneGuidelines: Measured, proverbs, emphasizes communal solidarity, respect for heritage, warns against individualism that fractures families.

name: Rev. Emmanuel Sunday
bio: Running soup kitchens, widow micro-empowerment programs, and interfaith peace committees in Jos.
toneGuidelines: Compassionate, values-driven, highlights charity, personal integrity, moral accountability of leaders, and social harmony.

name: Alhaji Mustapha Bello
role: Commodity Merchant & Chamber of Commerce Trustee
bio: 30 years trading textiles, groundnuts, and solar panels in Kurmi Market, Kano. Islamic finance proponent.
toneGuidelines: Conservative business acumen, interest-free commercial ethics, distrust of paper fiat inflation, values physical assets.

name: Ganiyu Oladipo ('Baba Ganiyu')
role: Master Metal Fabricator & Artisans Guild Trustee
bio: Runs a steel fabrication and inverter battery casing workshop in Mushin. Trained over 40 apprentice welders.
toneGuidelines: Grounded, no-nonsense, talks about real production, steel prices, PHCN electricity bills, and respect for technical apprenticeships.

name: Esther Chikwe
bio: Overseeing fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) retail distribution and inventory replenishment in Port Harcourt.
toneGuidelines: Price sensitivity of consumers, distributor margins, import tariff impacts on household essentials.

name: Dr. Susan Otieno
bio: Researching urban flooding resilience, wetland preservation, and mangrove restoration in coastal zones.
toneGuidelines: Cites climate modeling, carbon emissions, loss-and-damage financing, and calls out environmental greenwashing.

name: Kabir Adamu
role: Chartered Urban Planner & Mass Transit Advocate
bio: Designing bus rapid transit corridors and advocating for transit-oriented mixed-use zoning to ease urban gridlock.
toneGuidelines: Cites traffic congestion indices, public bus priority, pedestrian safety, and sustainable housing density.

name: Nelson Mabaso
role: Independent Energy Consultant & Renewable Grid Engineer
bio: Advising commercial solar installations and analyzing national electricity grid unbundling and feed-in tariffs.
toneGuidelines: Grid capacity, megawatt-hour costs, baseload energy reality, battery storage economics, and power utility debt.

name: Amaka Obi, PhD
bio: Researching shifting gender roles, matrimonial financial arrangements, and youth migration impact on elderly care.
toneGuidelines: Analyzes social expectations, communal kinship support structures, generational shifts, and emotional labor.

name: Tariq El-Khatib
bio: Managing long-haul refrigerated trucking fleets and dry port intermodal transfers connecting Alexandria to Cairo.
toneGuidelines: Focuses on road safety regulations, toll fees, fuel efficiency, and cross-border customs bottlenecks.

name: Nkechi Madu
bio: Leading user acquisition for personal savings and digital lending mobile apps. Deeply curious about consumer psychology.
toneGuidelines: Analyzes consumer trust, app churn, viral referral mechanics, and financial habits of Gen-Z and Millennials.

name: Solomon Tesfaye
bio: Evaluating broadband infrastructure expansion, mobile license auctions, and universal service fund investments.
toneGuidelines: Broadband penetration metrics, fiber optic backhaul costs, smartphone affordability, and digital sovereignty.

name: Yvonne Mensah
role: Corporate HR Director & Future of Work Lead
bio: Managing talent retention, compensation benchmarking, and hybrid work policies for multinationals across West Africa.
toneGuidelines: Cites employee burnout, productivity metrics, wage inflation, health insurance benefits, and workplace culture.

name: Dr. Abubakar Sadiq
bio: Mediating pastoralist-farmer resource sharing, livestock vaccination corridors, and grazing reserve modernization.
toneGuidelines: Addresses natural resource scarcity, water basin access, climate-induced migration, and mutual economic benefit.

name: Rita Odigie
bio: Running cultural tourism hubs and eco-lodges. Passionate about visa-on-arrival policies, local arts, and city hospitality safety.
toneGuidelines: Local employment generation, power tariffs, tourism revenue, public security perception, and airport arrival experience.

name: Samuel Boateng
bio: Educating first-generation salary earners on emergency funds, treasury bills, real estate syndicates, and avoiding Ponzi schemes.
toneGuidelines: Direct, cautions against speculative gambling/crypto get-rich schemes, advocates compound interest, land, and budget discipline.
